The working file is the complete analysis; the Markdown and PDF reports are reader copies of it. Each should be read in full — this message is only a pointer, not the analysis.

**Bottom line:** Don't launch an open, public free tier. Run a capped, gated, time-boxed pilot (hard signup cap, buyer-fit gating, a Finance-approved cost ceiling, pre-committed kill/hold/expand thresholds) plus a separate "free expansion seats" wedge inside existing paying accounts — and treat building full self-serve PLG infrastructure as a distinct, later decision. Overall confidence is **LOW**, honestly: six of the seven inputs are business-stipulated facts this analysis couldn't independently verify, the conversion rate is a genuine unknown by design, and the weighted trade-off itself came out a near-tie (82 vs. 81) that an option-value argument — not the scorecard — tips toward running the pilot. The sharpest findings: the business's all-outbound motion structurally forecloses the two usual freemium justifications (PLG growth engine, TOFU lead-gen) until separate infrastructure is built, and volume-capping — not guessing the conversion rate — is the actual near-term risk-control problem.
